who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), lane L5 ty-lower of the front-end-on-memo port, port-memo-1113
where: crates/hir-ty/src (lower.rs, lower/batch.rs, infer.rs, consteval*, layout*, providers.rs, opaques.rs, ...)
what: Porting hir-ty's queries to blaze-memo meant deciding, query by query, whether its value owns heap memory (ThinVec, Box<[..]>, SmallVec, ArenaMap, Box<str> in an error) and then either rewriting it to a kept slice or marking it `owns`. Nothing listed which values drop: it was read off each type and the types it holds, with no compiler to ask, since the lane runs nothing.
cost: the larger part of the lane's reading; the list of `owns` (about 60 queries) is a best reading that the first compile's no-drop asserts will correct
cause: query values were designed as owned trees (rust-analyzer's salsa heritage) and the engine never had to know whether a value drops
class: a property of a type (needs_drop) that a port has to know at every site but no tool reports before compiling
prevention: a reflection-derived report (`needs_drop` per tracked value type, by query name) the port can read before writing, and value types built as kept slices and records from the start so `owns` stays rare
workaround: read each value type and every field type it holds; mark `owns` where any field drops, convert the flat `Box<[Copy]>` ones to `keep_iter`/`keep_slice`
